title: LibRPA memory bottleneck: build against the LibRI fine_grain_lock branch
symptom: A LibRPA stage hits a memory bottleneck (OOM kill, very high peak RSS, or the scheduler memory cap) especially at large k-grid or auxiliary-basis sizes.
root_cause: The default LibRI build uses the coarse-grained lock layout; the LibRI `fine_grain_lock` branch provides a lower-memory include/interface for the same LibRPA calculation.
minimal_fix: Build LibRPA against that LibRI tree by pointing the include at the fine-grained-lock folder, for example: cmake -DLIBRI_INCLUDE_DIR=../LibRI-fine_grained_lock/include (path relative to the LibRPA build directory). Confirm the folder location on the target host before building; the local LibRI master does not contain this branch.
validation: Verify the configured include path is the fine_grain_lock tree, record the LibRI revision, and measure the peak RSS of the same LibRPA stage before and after the rebuild. Re-run the stage gate battery and the Coulomb check with the new build.
avoid: Do not point LIBRI_INCLUDE_DIR at a folder from a different LibRI revision, do not mix a fine-grained-lock LibRI with a LibRPA source built against another interface, and do not silently switch builds without recording the revision in provenance.
